edges.note: Both state that code is read far more than written, so clarity is judged from the reader.
Boy Scout Rule (leave each module cleaner) restates leaving the codebase healthier than found.
Avoiding name encodings and sizing names to scope is concrete guidance under intention-revealing naming.
Bundling related parameters into a parameter object is a mechanism for minimizing arguments.
Tiny behaviour-preserving steps with tests is the mechanism for refactoring when change demands it.
Keeping test code as clean as production code specializes keep-it-clean-continuously to tests.
A fast self-checking test suite is the safety net that makes tiny-step refactoring possible.
Risk-driven, bug-finding testing supports maintaining a trustworthy self-testing suite.
Intention-revealing names make intent visible, supporting readability.
Small, well-named functions that separate intention from implementation support readability.
Consistent formatting and newspaper-style file structure support readability.
Treating patterns as shared vocabulary and refactoring targets supports using patterns only where they reduce complexity.
Encapsulating mutable and global data supports composition-based OO design.
Redesigning when complexity appears supports minimizing long-term maintenance effort.
Building only as generic as present needs require supports minimizing long-term maintenance effort.
Refactoring when change demands it supports optimizing for changeability.
Writing clean code by successive refinement supports keeping code clean continuously.
Pattern enthusiasm (apply patterns, build a pattern vocabulary) can pull toward speculative generality, which the only-as-generic-as-present-needs rule rejects.
edges.resolution: Scope by present need: introduce a pattern only when a problem actually recurs now (refactor TO patterns), never speculatively. With that gate both rules agree.
